questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

The guard said to the visitors, "Do not take photographs inside the museum."

options.text: The guard warned the visitors not to be taking photographs inside the museum.
The guard forbade the visitors to take photographs inside the museum.
The guard told the visitors that do not take photographs inside the museum.
The guard requested the visitors to not took photographs inside the museum.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

The given sentence is an **imperative sentence in Direct speech.**

When we convert from **direct to indirect speech**, the following **changes** take place:

 
• The verb of the **reporting verb does not change.**
 
• Imperative changes in the infinitive form.
 
• It is a __negative sentence__ (do not) thus, **'said'** changes to **'forbade'. To forbid means not to allow something; order (someone) not to do something.**
 
• The verb takes the infinitive form 'to take'. 

Following the rules of conversion, the indirect speech sentence is: *The guard forbade the visitors to take photographs inside the museum.*

**When we convert a sentence from direct to indirect speech, we make the following changes:**

 
• **Quotation marks** are **omitted** and the sentence** ends with a full stop**. 
 
• The **tense** of the **verb**, in the reported speech involving any **order, request and instruction** does** not undergo** any **change **during the conversion from direct to indirect mode. This is also true if the statement is a** universal truth.** 
 
• If the** reporting verb** is in the **present tense**, it does **not undergo** any **change**.
 
• We add the word** 'to' **before the verb if the verb is in **bare infinitive**.
 
• When the reporting or **principal verb** is in the **present tense**, all present tenses of the direct are **changed** into the corresponding** past tenses.**
 
• Words expressing **nearness in time or place** are generally converted into words expressing** distance**.

 For eg.** now** becomes **then**,** today** becomes **that day**, **yesterday** becomes **the previous day**, **this** becomes** that,** etc.
 
• In reporting **commands and requests**, the** verb expressing command or request **is **added** and the** imperative **is changed into the** infinitive.** 
 
• In reporting** questions** the** verbs like asked, inquired** are **added** 
 
• In reporting** exclamations and wishes**, the** verbs expressing exclamation or wish** are **added**. 
 
• When we convert a sentence from the direct to the indirect mode(especially for a sentence** ending** with a** mark of interrogation**), we** reverse** the **subject-verb placement.** In **direct** sentences, we have the **verb before the subject**; while in** indirect,** the **verb follows the subject. **

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

He was greatly disappointed __to be failed __again.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

'to be failed' is incorrectly used. It must be replaced with the participle form 'on failing'.

**To fail **means having a lack of success, shortcoming, weakness.

Thus the correct sentence will be: *He was greatly disappointed on failing again.*

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

He went to work but returned back immediately.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

The error is in the part **'but returned back'.**

It is **redundant to use 'back' after 'returned'**. The word 'back' is implied by the word 'returned'.

Thus the correct sentence will be: *He went to work but returned immediately.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (1).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

 
• **Choice:** an act of choosing between two or more possibilities
 
• **Possibility:** a thing that may be chosen or done out of several possible alternatives.
 
• **Option:** a thing that is or may be chosen.
 
• **Alternative:** available as another possibility or choice.

The sentence talks about certain spheres of life and no other options suits better than **choice**.

Other options do not convey the meaning in the context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (2).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

**'Of'** is used to indicate a relation with non-living things.

 
• **'Among'** refers when talking about more than two things.
 
• **'Between'** refers to a relation between two things.

Other options thus do not fit in the context, grammatically and contextually.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

**'Unless'**, is **conditional conjunction**. It means except something.

Other conjunctions of cause and contrast make the sentence incorrect in the context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (4).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

**Should **expresses obligation. 

It states that if the person is not interested in the subject they must or should not opt for it.

Other modal auxiliary options are incorrect in the context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (5)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

**Square **is the correct answer. The idiomatic expression **square peg in a round hole **mean that one is in a situation of doing something which is not suitable for that person. 

Thus other options large, small, circular are incorrect in the sentence.

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

He incurred heavy losses in business.

options.text: Heavy losses are incurred in business by him.
Heavy losses were incurred in business by him.
Heavy losses are being incurred in business by him.
Heavy losses was incurred in business by him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

The given sentence is an **assertive statement in Active Voice**. Its structure is: **Subject + simple past tense + Indirect object + Direct Object.**

When we convert the sentence in **Passive Voice**, its structure will be: Indirect Object + were + simple past tense + Direct object + by + Subject (Objective case).</s

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The present what I buy for you yesterday was very expensive.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

The error is in the part 'what I buy'.

We see that 'yesterday' expresses the adverb of **time. **Hence simple past tense of the verb **'bought'** must be used.

Also the correct usage of **relative pronoun 'that'** must be used indicating back to 'the present'. 'What' is an incorrect usage.

Thus the correct sentence will be: *The present that I bought for you yesterday was very expensive.*
